title: Speculation and deduction
grammar: Modal verbs for deduction, Modal perfects
function: Speculate about the present and the past

sections.heading: Deduction in the present
sections.body: We use modal verbs to express how certain we are about something in the present. The choice of modal shows the strength of our deduction.

sections.heading: Deduction in the past: modal perfects
sections.body: To make deductions about the past we use modal + have + past participle.

sections.heading: Examples in context
list: The lights are off. They must have gone out.
She looks tired. She might have slept badly.
He passed the exam easily. He can't have studied hard.
I should have studied more. Now I regret it.
We would have come if you had invited us.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'must to have'. Say 'must have'.
Do not confuse 'must have' (deduction) with 'had to' (obligation).
Remember: 'can't have' means impossible, not 'mustn't have'.

list.definition: Apparently, they got married last year.
Clearly, someone has made a mistake.
It seems that they have already left.
There is no doubt he must have known.
If I had known, I would have helped.
In that case, he must have been late.
He must have run, otherwise he would be late.
Suppose she had missed the train.
Imagine you had won the lottery.
I'm sure she must have forgotten.
I'm certain he can't have done it.
I doubt they have arrived yet.
I wonder if he might have left.
It's possible that she has forgotten.
It's unlikely that they have finished.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: She must be at work. Her car is in the car park.
He might have forgotten our meeting.
They can't have arrived yet. It's too early.
You should have told me about the problem.
The lights are off. They must have gone out.
I would have helped you if you had asked.
She might be ill. She looks pale.
questions: In sentences 1, 5 and 7, what is the difference between 'must', 'might' and 'can't' for deduction?
In sentences 2, 3 and 5, which structure is used for deductions about the past?
In sentence 4, what does 'should have' express?
In sentence 6, what does 'would have' express?
In sentence 8, why do we use 'can't' and not 'mustn't'?

questions.prompt: The lights are off. They ___ gone out.
questions.explanation: When almost certain about the past, we use must have + past participle.

questions.prompt: She ___ the message. She was not at home.
questions.explanation: Cannot have + past participle expresses impossibility in the past.

questions.prompt: You ___ told me! Now it's too late.
questions.explanation: Should have expresses regret or criticism about the past.

questions.prompt: He ___ be tired. He worked all day.
questions.explanation: Strong deduction in the present: must.

questions.prompt: She ___ forgotten about the meeting. She is very organised.
questions.explanation: Impossibility in the past: can't have.

questions.prompt: I ___ helped you if you had asked.
questions.explanation: Hypothetical past: would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: It's very late. He ___ be at home already.
questions.explanation: Possibility: might.

questions.prompt: You look tired. You ___ slept badly.
questions.explanation: Deduction from evidence: must have.

questions.prompt: That ___ be John. He is on holiday.
questions.explanation: Impossibility in the present: can't.

questions.prompt: She ___ passed the exam without studying.
questions.explanation: Impossibility in the past: couldn't have.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Your neighbour is playing loud music at 2 am. Write 5 speculations about why using must, might, could, can't.
Look at a photo of a stranger. Write 5 deductions about their life (job, age, where they live) using modal verbs.
Think about a mistake you made recently. Write 5 sentences using should have, could have, would have, must have, can't have.

questions.prompt: The window is broken. Someone ___ broken in.
questions.explanation: Strong deduction about the past: must have.

questions.prompt: She ___ be at home. Her car is not there.
questions.explanation: Impossibility in the present: can't.

questions.prompt: You ___ told me you were coming! I would have cooked.
questions.explanation: Should have expresses criticism or regret.

questions.prompt: He ___ have taken the wrong bus. He is very late.
questions.explanation: Possibility in the past: might have.

questions.prompt: They ___ arrived yet. The flight was delayed.
questions.explanation: Impossibility: can't have.

questions.prompt: I ___ come to the party if I hadn't been ill.
questions.explanation: Hypothetical past: would have.

questions.prompt: She said she was tired. She ___ worked too much.
questions.explanation: Deduction: must have.

questions.prompt: That ___ be Mary. She is much taller.
questions.explanation: Impossibility in the present.

questions.prompt: I ___ studied harder. I failed the exam.
questions.explanation: Regret: should have.

questions.prompt: He ___ forgotten the appointment. He is usually very punctual.
questions.explanation: Impossibility based on evidence: can't have.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Present deduction: must (certain), might/may/could (possible), can't (impossible).
Past deduction: modal + have + past participle.
Must have: strong deduction about the past.
Can't have: impossible in the past.
Should have: regret or criticism.
Would have: hypothetical past.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'must to have'. Say 'must have'.
Do not use 'mustn't have'. Use 'can't have' for impossibility.
Do not confuse deduction (must) with obligation (have to).

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: She must have...
He can't have...
They might have...
You should have...
I would have...
It seems that...
There is no doubt that...
